metaDescription: Suspended or blocked license in El Paso? Attorney Robert Navar handles occupational licenses, OMNI holds, DWLI tickets and the path back to a full license.
h1: Driver's License Lawyer El Paso, TX
intro: Losing your license in El Paso means losing the way to work, school and Fort Bliss. Attorney Robert Navar helps drivers figure out why the license was suspended or blocked, get an occupational license to drive legally in the meantime, and clear the path back to a full license.
summaryHeading: First, find out why your license is suspended
summary: A Texas license is suspended or blocked for a short list of reasons: a DWI arrest or test refusal, driving without insurance, repeated moving-violation convictions, unresolved tickets through an OMNI hold, or child-support and other administrative actions. Each has a different fix.
An occupational driver's license under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L lets you drive for work, school and household needs while a suspension runs.
Driving on a suspended license is its own offense — driving while license invalid (DWLI), Transportation Code §521.457 — and a conviction can extend the suspension. Get the ODL first.

If DPS will not renew rather than having suspended you, the problem is usually an OMNI hold from an old ticket. The consultation is free: schedule an appointment or call 915-503-1600 and bring your DPS notice.

sections.heading: Three Different Problems That All Look Like "My License Is Gone"
paragraphs: Most license problems we see in El Paso fall into three buckets, and the DPS letter does not make the difference obvious. The first is an administrative or court-ordered suspension: a DWI arrest, a breath or blood test refusal, a crash without insurance, a medical or child-support action, or a suspension DPS imposes for repeated moving-violation convictions. Texas no longer uses the former Driver Responsibility Program points system, but repeated convictions can still affect a driver's record and may lead to suspension in some circumstances. These suspensions have lengths set by statute or by the court.

The second bucket is not technically a suspension at all. An OMNI hold under Transportation Code Chapter 706 means a court reported an unpaid ticket or missed date, and DPS will not renew the license until that court clears it. The third is an expired license that cannot be renewed because of a hold, which is how people end up with a no driver's license ticket on top of everything else. The first thing we do in a consultation is pull your DPS record and figure out which one you actually have — many drivers have two or three stacked on top of each other.

sections.heading: Driving Legally During a Suspension: the Occupational License
paragraphs: An occupational driver's license (ODL) is a court order under Transportation Code Chapter 521, Subchapter L that lets a suspended driver operate a non-commercial vehicle for work, school and essential household duties. We file a petition in the appropriate El Paso County court, attach proof of SR-22 insurance and a certified driving record, and ask the judge to sign an order setting the hours, days, counties and purposes you may drive. Under the statute the signed order itself serves as your license for a limited period while DPS issues the card.

The ODL matters because the alternative is driving anyway. A driving while license invalid ticket is generally a Class C offense the first time and can become a Class B with a prior conviction, a crash or no insurance — and a DWLI conviction can extend the suspension. The ODL page has the full paperwork checklist.

sections.heading: Getting Back to a Full License
paragraphs: Reinstatement depends on what caused the problem. For an OMNI hold, the court must send DPS a clearance after the ticket is resolved; our OMNI hold removal page explains how we resolve the underlying case — pursuing a dismissal or deferred disposition so it adds no conviction — and ask the court to send the clearance so you can renew. For a conviction-based suspension, the suspension period has to run and DPS reinstatement fees have to be paid; in the meantime we defend any new ticket so nothing adds to the record. For a DWI or refusal suspension, the ODL carries you through the period.

A few things make reinstatement slower than it needs to be: an SR-22 that lapses mid-suspension, a second court's OMNI hold nobody noticed, or an unpaid reinstatement fee sitting in the DPS system. We check all three before telling a client the license is clear. If you already picked up a no driver's license or DWLI citation while suspended, those are often negotiable once a valid ODL is in hand — though no outcome can be promised.

sections.heading: Which Page You Need, and What to Send Us
paragraphs: If your license is already suspended and you need to drive, go to occupational driver's license. If DPS said it cannot renew because of a court hold, go to OMNI hold removal. If you were ticketed for driving on a suspended license, see driving while license invalid. If a pending ticket is what threatens the license, defend it now through our traffic tickets hub or the free lookup form.

Whichever page fits, send the office the DPS notice or renewal denial, a photo of the front of your license, your insurance card, and any citation or court mail you still have. Fort Bliss soldiers whose on-post driving privileges depend on a valid Texas license should say so, because the timing matters. Se habla español. This page is general information, not legal advice about your case — the consultation is free, so call 915-503-1600 and we will look at your record together.

faqs.q: Can I get an occupational license in El Paso if my license is suspended for DWI?
faqs.a: Often, yes. There may be a waiting period depending on prior offenses, and the court may require an ignition interlock, but ODLs are commonly granted for DWI-related suspensions. See our occupational driver's license page for the details.

faqs.q: What happens if I drive while my license is suspended?
faqs.a: You can be cited for driving while license invalid under Transportation Code §521.457. A first offense is generally a Class C misdemeanor; with a prior conviction, a crash or no insurance it can be a Class B with possible jail. A conviction can also extend the suspension. An ODL avoids that risk.

faqs.q: My license is fine but DPS won't renew it. What is going on?
faqs.a: That usually points to an OMNI hold — a court reported an unpaid ticket or missed appearance. The ticket has to be resolved and the court has to send DPS a clearance. We handle both; see OMNI hold removal.

faqs.q: How much does license help cost?
faqs.a: The consultation is free. An occupational license is a flat fee quoted after we see your record, plus the court filing fee and your SR-22. Clearing an OMNI hold is priced like any ticket: $59 in El Paso Municipal Court, $69 in JP and the smaller city courts, plus $35 if there is a warrant.
